mechanism: Mibavademab is an investigational fully human monoclonal antibody agonist that binds to and activates the leptin receptor (LEPR), a pathway involved in food intake, energy expenditure, and glucose/lipid metabolism. It is not structurally related to endogenous leptin, which may reduce the risk of anti-drug antibodies cross-reacting with and neutralizing endogenous leptin.
development_status: NCT06548100 is an active, not recruiting Phase 3 single-arm open-label safety study in 9 pediatric and adult generalized lipodystrophy participants switching from at least 6 months of metreleptin to mibavademab; estimated primary completion is July 14, 2026 and estimated study completion is November 3, 2026. A separate randomized Phase 3 LAGO efficacy/safety study, NCT07220785, is recruiting with estimated primary completion May 19, 2028 and estimated study completion September 8, 2028. FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy designation in generalized lipodystrophy in 2024 and orphan drug designation for treatment of lipodystrophy in 2025; FDA orphan approval status remains not approved.
clinical_summary: Generalized lipodystrophy is an ultra-rare leptin-deficiency disorder with severe diabetes and hypertriglyceridemia risk. Mibavademab targets the same leptin axis as metreleptin but via LEPR agonism rather than leptin replacement, and Regeneron states it is being developed for generalized lipodystrophy. In the completed Phase 2 GLD study (NCT04159415), low-dose Week 8 primary endpoint results were mixed versus placebo, but a 2025 Journal of the Endocrine Society abstract reported that 8 patients treated with high-dose mibavademab for up to 52 weeks had mean HbA1c reduction of 2.12 percentage points and median fasting triglyceride reduction of 74.6%. The evidence supports meaningful differentiation because of the novel LEPR agonist mechanism, Breakthrough Therapy status, potential antibody-risk advantage versus metreleptin, and high-dose metabolic signal, but the data remain small and Phase 3 results are pending.
safety_summary: NCT06548100 is designed primarily to assess treatment-emergent adverse-event incidence and severity through Week 68, with pharmacokinetics and anti-drug/neutralizing antibodies as secondary outcomes. In posted NCT04159415 results, there were no deaths across treatment periods; serious adverse events occurred in some later open-label periods, and common non-serious events varied across small groups. The 2025 high-dose abstract described mibavademab as generally well tolerated. Key safety uncertainties include long-term immunogenicity, neutralizing antibodies, metabolic instability during switching from metreleptin, hypoglycemia when diabetes medications are adjusted, cardiovascular/renal exclusions in trials, and whether any label will need Myalept-like REMS or lymphoma/neutralizing-antibody monitoring.
management_tools: Specialty-drug prior authorization with diagnosis confirmation for congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy
Require documentation of leptin-deficiency manifestations such as hyperinsulinemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, severe insulin resistance, hypertriglyceridemia, or pancreatitis risk
Endocrinologist, geneticist, or lipodystrophy-specialist prescribing or consultation requirement
Baseline and continuation criteria using HbA1c, fasting triglycerides, insulin dose, pancreatitis history, liver/metabolic markers, and tolerability
Benefit-placement review for IV loading dose plus ongoing subcutaneous maintenance dosing
Quantity limits and refill controls aligned to final labeled dose, loading schedule, and vial/syringe presentation
Transition-of-care criteria for patients switching from metreleptin, including avoidance of duplicate leptin-axis therapy unless supported by label
Medical exception pathway for patients with metreleptin neutralizing antibodies, loss of efficacy, intolerance, or REMS access barriers
evidence_gaps: No commercial mibavademab price, WAC, net-cost estimate, or final dosing presentation has been disclosed.
NCT06548100 is a small single-arm switch/safety study with 9 enrolled participants and no posted results.
The randomized Phase 3 LAGO study (NCT07220785) has no posted efficacy or safety results and is not expected to reach primary completion until May 2028.

Clinical evidence in GLD remains based on very small Phase 2 datasets and conference abstract data; durability, comparative efficacy versus metreleptin, and pediatric outcomes require Phase 3 confirmation.

Final U.S. label language is unknown, including whether mibavademab will be positioned for treatment-naive use, metreleptin switch use, metreleptin failure/intolerance, pediatric subgroups, or all GLD patients.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06548100 points to expanded access NCT07502716, but that NCT record appears to describe ubamatamab compassionate use rather than mibavademab.

sources.title: A Study of the Safety of Mibavademab in Pediatric and Adult Participants Switching From Metreleptin to Mibavademab for the Treatment of Generalized Lipodystrophy (GLD)
supports: Official title describes a single-arm, open-label safety study in generalized lipodystrophy patients switching from metreleptin to mibavademab, a leptin receptor agonist antibody.
Sponsor is Regeneron Pharmaceuticals; intervention is mibavademab/REGN4461 administered by IV infusion followed by subcutaneous injection.
Status is active, not recruiting; Phase 3; actual enrollment 9; actual start December 16, 2024; estimated primary completion July 14, 2026; estimated completion November 3, 2026.
Primary outcomes are incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events through Week 68.
Secondary outcomes include HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, insulin dose, fasting triglycerides, serum mibavademab concentration, anti-drug antibodies, and neutralizing antibodies.

sources.title: Efficacy and Safety of Mibavademab in Adult and Pediatric Patients With Generalized Lipodystrophy
supports: LAGO is a two-part randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 study of mibavademab efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics in generalized lipodystrophy.
Sponsor is Regeneron Pharmaceuticals; intervention is mibavademab/REGN4461.
Recruiting; estimated enrollment 28; actual start March 13, 2026; estimated primary completion May 19, 2028; estimated study completion September 8, 2028.
Part A primary outcomes include change in HbA1c and percent change in fasting triglycerides through 36 weeks of exposure to mibavademab.
Part B primary outcomes include treatment-emergent adverse events, severity of TEAEs, and serum mibavademab concentrations up to 15 months.

sources.title: Study of REGN4461, a Leptin Receptor Agonist Antibody, in Patients With Generalized Lipodystrophy
supports: Completed randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 study of REGN4461/mibavademab in generalized lipodystrophy with actual enrollment 16.
Primary objectives assessed glycemic parameters in participants with HbA1c >=7% and fasting triglycerides in participants with TG >=250 mg/dL.

Week 8 primary posted results showed HbA1c change -0.1 for placebo versus 0.2 for low-dose REGN4461, fasting glucose change 15.5 versus 53.6 mg/dL, weighted mean glucose change -3.7 versus -3.7, and fasting TG percent change -6.0% versus 11.8%.
No deaths were reported in posted adverse-event results; serious adverse events occurred in later treatment periods in small groups.

sources.title: SUN-253 The Impact of Mibavademab, a Novel Leptin Receptor Agonist, on Metabolic Parameters in Individuals with Generalized Lipodystrophy
supports: Mibavademab is described as an investigational human leptin receptor agonist monoclonal antibody that is not structurally related to endogenous leptin and activates LEPR with or without leptin present.
Sixteen GLD patients with baseline diabetes or hypertriglyceridemia completed at least 28 weeks of mibavademab treatment in NCT04159415.
Eight patients entered the high-dose open-label period and received a median 51 high-dose doses over median 49.9 weeks.
After 52 weeks of high-dose treatment, mean HbA1c change was -2.12 percentage points and median fasting TG percent change was -74.6%.
The abstract states high-dose mibavademab was generally well tolerated and associated with sustained, clinically meaningful metabolic improvements.

sources.title: DailyMed - MYALEPT (metreleptin) Prescribing Information
supports: MYALEPT is indicated as adjunct to diet as replacement therapy to treat complications of leptin deficiency in congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy.
Recommended adult starting dose is 2.5 mg daily for males over 40 kg and 5 mg daily for females over 40 kg, with maximum daily dose 10 mg.
MYALEPT is administered once daily; each vial contains 11.3 mg metreleptin and can be used for multiple doses within 3 days when reconstituted with bacteriostatic water.
Boxed warning covers anti-metreleptin antibodies with neutralizing activity and risk of lymphoma; MYALEPT is available only through a REMS.

Common adverse reactions in GLD trials included headache, hypoglycemia, decreased weight, and abdominal pain; label reports 1-year mean HbA1c reduction of 2 percentage points and median fasting triglyceride percent change of -55% in an open-label GLD study.

sources.title: Myalept Prices, Coupons, Copay Cards & Patient Assistance
supports: Myalept 11.3 mg subcutaneous powder for injection is listed from $6,296.67 for one powder for injection.
Myalept is commonly used for lipodystrophy.
Public price source does not represent negotiated payer net cost, rebates, or patient assistance.

sources.title: Lipodystrophy - Myalept Prior Authorization Policy
supports: Prior authorization is recommended for prescription benefit coverage of Myalept.
Policy notes Myalept is the only drug specifically indicated for treatment of lipodystrophy and first-line for metabolic/endocrine abnormalities in generalized lipodystrophy.
Coverage criteria require congenital or acquired generalized lipodystrophy, manifestation of leptin deficiency, dietary modification, and endocrinologist or geneticist prescribing or consultation.
Manifestations of leptin deficiency include hyperinsulinemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertriglyceridemia.

expected_launch_window.method: Used the active Phase 3 switch/safety study completing in 2026, the randomized Phase 3 LAGO primary completion in May 2028, and FDA Breakthrough Therapy plus orphan designation to estimate a filing/review window after Phase 3 data.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A U.S. launch before 2029 is unlikely because the randomized efficacy study is not expected to complete primary follow-up until May 2028, but Breakthrough Therapy and orphan status could support an expedited review path if results are positive.

annual_cost_range.method: Used Myalept as the disease-specific analog. Low estimate assumes adult male starting dose 2.5 mg daily, one 11.3 mg vial lasting up to 3 days after bacteriostatic-water reconstitution: ceil(365/3) x $6,296.67 = $768,194. High estimate assumes adult maximum 10 mg daily requiring approximately one vial per day: 365 x $6,296.67 = $2,298,285.
annual_cost_range.explanation: Mibavademab has no disclosed price or final presentation. The estimate is a gross drug-acquisition analog before rebates, patient assistance, wastage beyond label assumptions, IV loading administration, specialist visits, metabolic monitoring, or adverse-event costs.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation, orphan status, novel LEPR agonist mechanism, potential non-cross-reactive antibody advantage versus leptin replacement, and high-dose Phase 2 metabolic improvements against small samples and pending randomized Phase 3 results.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Mibavademab could address important limitations of metreleptin and may offer strong metabolic benefit, but evidence is still limited to small Phase 2 and ongoing Phase 3 studies.

budget_impact.method: Balanced very high analog per-patient annual cost and chronic therapy against the ultra-rare GLD population, existing Myalept management framework, and likely specialist-controlled use.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient spend could be substantial, but population-level budget impact should be moderated by rarity and by substitution for an already expensive standard of care in many patients.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed from Phase 3 status, Breakthrough Therapy/orphan designations, potential switch from metreleptin, IV loading plus SC maintenance logistics, and pending 2028 randomized data.
disruption_risk.explanation: The asset is clinically credible and may change GLD treatment pathways, but disruption is contained by a small eligible population and non-immediate launch timing.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects Phase 3 development, regulatory designations, high analog cost, and the availability of Myalept PA criteria that can be adapted for mibavademab launch planning.
recommended_action.explanation: Begin preparing diagnosis, specialist, metabolic-manifestation, continuation, and switch criteria now; defer final formulary positioning and contract strategy until Phase 3 results, label, dosing, and price are available.

quality_flags: Mibavademab is investigational and not FDA-approved for the orphan indication as of the FDA orphan designation record checked for this packet.
No direct mibavademab price is available; annual cost is analog-derived from Myalept public pricing and dosing assumptions.
The assigned NCT06548100 study is a small single-arm switch/safety study and should be interpreted alongside the separate randomized Phase 3 LAGO efficacy/safety study NCT07220785.
Posted NCT04159415 low-dose Week 8 primary endpoint results are mixed, while high-dose efficacy is currently supported by a small open-label extension/conference abstract dataset.
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06548100 lists expanded access NCT07502716, but that NCT record appears to be for ubamatamab compassionate use and may be an unrelated CT.gov linkage issue.
